title: Evening Edition
notes: Evening Edition for Thursday, Nov 12, 2026, published on request. It is a one-off and does not change the regular morning schedule.

It prioritizes developments since this morning’s edition. Nvidia’s board had not announced a decision this morning; the company later said it had accepted Jensen Huang’s resignation. The Brooklyn collapse death toll rose to eight, search-and-rescue ended, and the NYPD named the victims. U.S. envoys met Putin in Moscow and then Zelenskyy in Dublin. Ottawa served Stellantis a default notice after a Thursday meeting in Toronto.

A few China and Hong Kong official or market items were released during the U.S. overnight or early morning and were not in the morning edition; they are included here and dated accordingly. Thursday’s Hong Kong and Shanghai closes came before Nvidia announced the resignation in the U.S.

The second trial voyage of Adora Flora City (Nov 14–16), the start of its season from Guangzhou on Nov 22, the Hong Kong Sun Yat-sen exhibition’s public opening on Friday, registration for Cantonese Opera Day workshops, the world juniors in Alberta, Nvidia’s Nov 17 earnings, and a possible E.U. discussion of a special envoy are described as scheduled or under consideration. Tretiak’s compensation demand and the criminal charges in the Kai Tak case are allegations or claims, not proven facts.
This edition has photos on the lead and on 20 of 21 stories, using only Wikimedia Commons or public-domain files, each credited and labelled as a file photo.
provenance: Stories are compiled from the linked sources; labels describe the type of claim each story rests on.
Source pages were opened during this evening’s research between about 9:08 and 9:25 PM ET; each check time is the logged time that page was fetched.

Xinhua, China Daily and People’s Daily (Chongqing Daily) items are labelled State media. The Kremlin transcript is an official Russian government publication. Some Reuters reporting was read in a Business Recorder republication; the Wall Street Journal and New York Times are cited only as relayed by other outlets.

CBC published a correction at 8:32 PM ET on the amount of Stellantis subsidies discussed in earlier coverage; this edition uses the corrected figures. Brooklyn victim names come from the NYPD as reported by ABC7 on Thursday evening; an earlier BBC account said officials had not yet identified them. Where outlets gave different injury counts, this edition uses the FDNY/ABC7 and BBC figure of 18.

stories.headline: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO; CFO Colette Kress named interim chief
stories.deck: Nvidia said Thursday that its board had accepted co-founder Jensen Huang’s resignation as president, CEO and a director, effective immediately, and named chief financial officer Colette Kress as interim CEO. Shares finished 4.3% lower after falling as much as 13% at the open.
stories.summary: Nvidia said Thursday that its board had accepted co-founder Jensen Huang’s resignation as president, chief executive and a member of the board, effective immediately, and appointed chief financial officer Colette Kress as interim CEO. A Form 8-K filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission said the board accepted the resignation on Nov. 11 and also named longtime director Harvey C. Jones, a former Synopsys chief executive, as the company’s first board chair. Kress, 59, has been finance chief since 2013 and will keep that job while a search for a permanent CEO considers internal and external candidates. Nvidia’s statement thanked Huang for 33 years at the company and said it still plans to report fiscal third-quarter results on Nov. 17. CNBC said the shares closed down 4.3%, after sliding more than 13% at the open, and remained above a $4 trillion market value by the close. The resignation follows reports, denied by Beijing, that U.S. intelligence considers Alice Huang, a woman with whom he had a relationship, a Chinese intelligence asset, and a New York Times report, cited by CNBC and others, of a second relationship with Nvidia vice president Kimberly Powell. CNBC, citing the Times, also said President Donald Trump called Huang on Tuesday and urged him to fight to keep his job, and later called the episode a “horrible thing.”
stories.why: Huang built the company that supplies most of the chips behind the AI boom, so a sudden leadership change at one of the world’s most valuable firms feeds straight into markets, U.S.–China technology policy and the investigations already under way — and this morning’s edition had to leave the board meeting unresolved.
stories.label: Reported + official statement + unnamed sources + allegation
stories.note: Ongoing story: this morning’s edition reported that the board had met and that no decision had been announced. The spying allegation comes from U.S. intelligence assessments reported by news outlets; it has not been proven, and China has denied it. The Trump phone call was reported by the New York Times and is relayed here from CNBC. Kress’s age and Jones’s background are from the SEC filing.

stories.headline: Eight dead, including two children, as Brooklyn collapse search ends and victims are named
stories.deck: The death toll from Wednesday’s building collapse in Flatbush rose to eight, including two children, and the FDNY said search-and-rescue work has ended. On Thursday evening the NYPD released the names of all eight people killed.
stories.summary: Eight people — six adults and two children — were killed and 18 others were injured when a three-storey building at 1321 Flatbush Avenue in Brooklyn collapsed into a neighboring excavation on Wednesday afternoon, Mayor Zohran Mamdani and the FDNY said. Six people were pronounced dead at the scene and two died in hospital; two of the dead were construction workers. ABC7, citing officials, said rescue operations have concluded and the site has been turned over to the Department of Buildings and the NYPD, who say there are no further victims. On Thursday evening the NYPD released the names of the eight people killed: Nicole Daniela Salvada Rodriguez, 9; Kevin Santiago Reyes Gonzalez, 10; Gabriel Siguencia, 22; Barry Mamadou, 23; Jose Luis Caguana Cosquillo, 26; Edgar Sapon, 26; Juan Daniel Salvada Guzman, 31; and Ndiaye Mamadou, 31. Mamdani said the dead included immigrants from Mexico, Colombia, Ecuador, Trinidad and elsewhere. The Department of Buildings has issued a stop-work order at the adjoining site at 2625 Bedford Avenue, where the developer had an active permit for excavation and foundation work; officials said a March stop-work order at that site was later lifted. The cause remains under investigation. Brooklyn District Attorney Eric Gonzalez has said prosecutors are examining whether any criminal conduct contributed to the collapse. Four of the injured are firefighters, the BBC reported, and one person was still in hospital in a critical condition.
stories.why: The casualty count has risen since this morning’s edition, the search is over, and the official naming of the victims turns a still-moving disaster story into a clearer account of who was lost — while investigators have not said what caused the collapse.
stories.label: Reported + official statement
stories.note: Ongoing story: this morning’s edition reported at least four dead and 17 injured, with figures still changing. This account uses the FDNY, mayoral and ABC7 figure of eight dead and 18 injured. An earlier BBC report, written before the NYPD released names, said officials had not yet identified the victims.

stories.headline: D.C. doctor kills building manager in Logan Circle gym shooting, then dies after barricade
stories.deck: Police say doctor Matt Wade Lambert, 55, fatally shot building manager James Stuart, 46, at a gym in Washington’s Logan Circle, wounded four other people and later died of a self-inflicted gunshot wound after barricading himself in his apartment.
stories.summary: A doctor locked in a long dispute over mould and other conditions in his Washington apartment fatally shot his building’s manager at a gym, wounded four other people and then killed himself, police said. The shooting began on Thursday morning inside a gym in an apartment building in Logan Circle, about a mile north of the White House. Building manager James Stuart, 46, was pronounced dead at the scene; four others were taken to hospital, and police said one of the injured was in a critical condition. Police identified the suspect as 55-year-old doctor Matt Wade Lambert. Interim Metropolitan Police Chief Jefferey Carroll said Lambert then barricaded himself in an apartment, fired through the door at officers at least twice, and later died of what appeared to be a self-inflicted gunshot wound after negotiators heard a shot and he stopped communicating. Carroll said police believe the attack was related to an ongoing dispute and a civil case Lambert had filed against the building’s condominium association and management over maintenance issues, including mould. After the gym shooting, police said, he fired from a seventh-floor patio at four people on the ground level. Officers recovered three firearms from the apartment, none registered to him in the District, and found containers of flammable liquid; Carroll said there appeared to be “some level of planning.” Mayor Muriel Bowser called it a “senseless act of gun violence” and said the White House had been briefed.
stories.why: The shooting, a mile from the White House, left a building manager dead and four people wounded, and police have tied it to a bitter maintenance dispute rather than a random attack.
stories.label: Reported + official statement
stories.note: The account of Lambert’s earlier comments about mould and an unliveable penthouse comes from the BBC, citing the Washington Sun; those remarks were not independently confirmed here. Police have not said how he obtained the firearms.

stories.headline: Stephen Curry out at least two weeks after tearing an oblique in loss to Houston
stories.deck: Golden State said Stephen Curry will miss at least two weeks after an MRI confirmed an oblique abdominal tear suffered in Wednesday’s loss to the Rockets. Coach Steve Kerr said “concern is high,” and ESPN, citing sources, said the team is bracing for an absence closer to a month.
stories.summary: Stephen Curry will miss at least two weeks after suffering an oblique abdominal tear, the Golden State Warriors said on Thursday. Curry left Wednesday’s loss to the Houston Rockets with 6:25 remaining in the first quarter and later had an MRI. ESPN’s Anthony Slater, with additional reporting from Shams Charania, wrote that Curry began grabbing at his right side early in the game, hit a 28-foot 3-pointer and yelled in pain after the release. Coach Steve Kerr said Curry told him it was an injury he had not felt before and that “concern is high.” Curry will miss at least the next seven games, against San Antonio, New Orleans, Dallas, Memphis, Boston, Sacramento and Portland, until he is re-evaluated. Sources told Charania that the Warriors are bracing for their star to be out closer to a month. The Warriors are 8-4 after the defeat snapped an eight-game winning streak. Curry is averaging 27.8 points in 26.3 minutes and shooting 45.7% from 3-point range, a career high. The team is already without starting wings Jimmy Butler III and Moses Moody, who are rehabbing knee injuries.
stories.why: Curry has been the engine of a hot Warriors start, so even a short absence changes the Western Conference picture, and the team itself is treating the injury as more than a minor tweak.
stories.label: Reported + official statement + unnamed sources
stories.note: The official timeline is “at least two weeks” until a re-evaluation. The suggestion that the absence could last closer to a month comes from unnamed sources cited by ESPN and is not a team announcement.

stories.headline: Joly serves Stellantis a default notice and says it owes “hundreds of millions,” after the company offers $24 million
stories.deck: After a Thursday meeting in Toronto, Industry Minister Mélanie Joly told Stellantis it is in default of a 2022 funding agreement and has 30 days to take corrective action. Stellantis said it would repay $24 million in federal subsidies; Joly said the company “is on the hook for hundreds of millions of dollars.”
stories.summary: Industry Minister Mélanie Joly said Thursday she is “fed up” with Stellantis after meeting company, Unifor and Ontario Premier Doug Ford’s representatives in Toronto about the planned sale of the idled Brampton, Ont., assembly plant to armoured-vehicle maker Roshel Inc. In a letter the same day she told Stellantis Canada CEO Trevor Longley that Ottawa is ending a resolution process and that the automaker is in default of a 2022 funding agreement. “Basically they have 30 days or else, of course, we’ll sue them,” she told reporters, and said the company “is on the hook for hundreds of millions of dollars” without naming a figure. In a Thursday statement reported by CBC, Longley said the company will return $24 million in federal subsidies. CBC said government records have previously shown roughly $220 million in subsidies to upgrade Stellantis plants in Ontario, and it later corrected earlier wording that had attributed that figure to the company. A Stellantis spokesperson, LouAnn Gosselin, had said the company would voluntarily repay support received for the Brampton retooling but declined to comment on the amount, citing confidentiality. The 2022 federal commitment was for up to $529 million to retool the Brampton and Windsor plants; Ontario committed $513 million. Joly’s letter, as quoted by The Canadian Press, said the Roshel transaction shows Stellantis is “no longer diligently working in good faith,” that she had not indicated support for the sale, and that the sale is expected to close by the end of this year. She said she intends to meet Stellantis’s global CEO, Antonio Filosa. Unifor national president Lana Payne said the plant “is sold,” that the union did not hear in Thursday’s meeting that governments would reverse it, and that a strike remains a last resort even after members voted 97.3% for a strike mandate. Prime Minister Mark Carney, speaking in Dublin, said being informed of “some aspects” of the sale was not the same as a “global solution” for the workers and again called a partial solution “a betrayal.” Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre, speaking in Calgary, asked whether the funding deal contained a job guarantee and who would be held responsible if it did not.
stories.why: The Thursday meeting this morning’s edition could only flag as scheduled has now produced a formal default notice, and the gap between a $24 million company offer and the minister’s “hundreds of millions” sets up a fight over public money and the future of a major Ontario plant.
stories.label: Reported + official statement
stories.note: Ongoing story: this morning’s edition reported that Joly was set to meet Stellantis, Unifor and Ontario. CBC published a correction at 8:32 PM ET clarifying that a $220 million figure came from the government’s public accounts, not from Stellantis. The company’s offer is $24 million; Joly has not specified the amount she says is owed.

stories.headline: Blue Jays apologize for Anthony Santander’s anti-Muslim posts after meeting community leaders
stories.deck: The Toronto Blue Jays apologized Thursday to the Muslim community and to fans for “pain and harm” caused by outfielder Anthony Santander’s social media posts. Santander has not publicly commented, and the club has not said whether he will be disciplined.
stories.summary: The Toronto Blue Jays apologized Thursday to the Muslim community and the team’s fans after outfielder Anthony Santander shared anti-Muslim posts last week and deleted them two days later. Team president and CEO Mark Shapiro said in a statement that officials had met that day with leaders in Toronto’s Muslim communities. “We condemn Islamophobia and all forms of hate,” Shapiro said, and he said the club was “deeply sorry” for the harm the posts had caused. The Canadian Press reported that the posts, shared after last week’s U.S. midterm elections, included a preacher saying “there is no such thing as kind Muslims” and another suggesting Sharia law would be imposed after Abdul El-Sayed was elected to the Senate in Michigan. General manager Ross Atkins, speaking Tuesday at MLB’s GM meetings, said he had asked Santander to address the controversy publicly; as of Thursday evening the player and his agency had not responded to messages, CP said. Steven Zhou of the National Council of Canadian Muslims called the roughly hour-long meeting “a positive step” and said there was a commitment to training for the player, but he said the next step should be an apology from Santander himself. It remained unclear whether the club would discipline him. Santander signed a five-year, US$92.5 million contract with Toronto in January 2025 and did not play at the major-league level last season because of injuries.
stories.why: Canada’s only major-league baseball team is trying to contain damage from a star player’s posts in a city where about one in 10 residents identify as Muslim, and the club’s apology still leaves the player himself silent.
stories.label: Reported + official statement
stories.note: The description of the deleted posts is from The Canadian Press. Whether any contract or social-media policy will be enforced had not been announced when this edition was compiled.

stories.headline: Ottawa looks at refrigerating a stretch of the Rideau Canal to keep the skateway open
stories.deck: The National Capital Commission’s CEO said Thursday the agency is pursuing a plan to embed refrigeration pipes in a roughly 900-metre stretch of the Rideau Canal, from the Corktown Footbridge to the National Arts Centre, after warm winters left the skateway unreliable.
stories.summary: National Capital Commission CEO Tobi Nussbaum told CBC Radio’s Ottawa Morning on Thursday that the Crown corporation is “going to pursue” artificially freezing the northern, downtown end of the Rideau Canal Skateway, though he said much more work remains on the details. The idea comes from a feasibility study that recommends refrigeration pipes in a concrete slab, similar to outdoor rinks, along about 900 metres from the Corktown Footbridge at Somerset Street West to the National Arts Centre — the busiest and, Nussbaum said, the hardest stretch to freeze naturally. He said refrigerating that section could triple the number of days it is open for skating. The 7.8-kilometre skateway, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, has mostly relied on natural ice since the NCC began clearing it in 1971. It did not open at all in 2023, opened for only 10 days the following year, and did not open last year after a warm, wet winter, CBC reported, before conditions rebounded in the next two seasons. A 2021 analysis commissioned by the NCC put the average season at around 46 days; another study has predicted fewer than 20 skating days by the 2050s unless greenhouse-gas emissions fall sharply. Nussbaum said it is too early to know the cost, which would be beyond what the NCC could afford on its own, and that the soonest such a system could be installed would be the early 2030s.
stories.why: The canal is one of Canada’s best-known winter landmarks, and the commission is now treating mechanical freezing — not just a milder climate — as the practical way to keep a stretch of it skateable.
stories.label: Official statement + reported
stories.note: This is a plan the NCC says it will pursue, not a funded construction decision. Cost, design and a timetable earlier than the early 2030s had not been set.

stories.headline: Tretiak says Russia will seek compensation if barred from the world juniors in Alberta
stories.deck: Russian hockey federation president Vladislav Tretiak said Thursday that if Russia cannot play at next month’s world junior championship, it will seek compensation from Canada and press to move, cancel or sanction the tournament. Ottawa confirmed Wednesday that Russian players will not be allowed to compete.
stories.summary: Vladislav Tretiak, president of the Russian ice hockey federation, said Thursday that Russia will seek compensation from Canada and push for the relocation or cancellation of next month’s world junior championship in Edmonton and Red Deer, or for sanctions on Canada, if Russian players are barred from competing. The comments, reported by the Russian state news agency TASS and relayed by The Canadian Press, came a day after Ottawa confirmed that Russian players would not be permitted to compete, even if they hold valid Canadian visas. Tretiak also told TASS that Russia would seek compensation from Germany, host of the 2027 men’s world championship, if denied a place there, and that the federation had asked the IIHF ethics council to investigate national federations organizing boycotts of games against Russia. “The IIHF has a way out — either allow us to participate or, if we cannot enter Canada, move the championship, not hold it at all or impose sanctions on Canada,” he said, according to the CP translation. Several federations, including Finland, Sweden, Czechia and Norway, have said their teams will refuse to face Russia. The dispute follows an Oct. 30 ruling by the Court of Arbitration for Sport ordering the IIHF to allow Russian teams into five tournaments, starting with the world juniors on Dec. 26. The IIHF had not formally announced a change to the 10-team field, CP said, and its website still listed Norway among the participants. Norway has said the IIHF told it Russia would be added at Norway’s expense, and that it still hopes to compete.
stories.why: A legal ruling, a Canadian government ban and now an explicit Russian threat to blow up the tournament have turned a junior hockey championship in Alberta into a diplomatic standoff with no settlement in sight.
stories.label: Claim + reported + official statement + state media
stories.note: Ongoing story: this morning’s edition reported Ottawa’s confirmation that Russian players would be barred. Tretiak’s compensation demand and call to move or cancel the event are claims by the Russian federation, reported via TASS. The IIHF had not announced a cancellation or relocation when this edition was compiled.

stories.headline: Hang Seng falls 1.3% as investors weigh the Nvidia scandal; Alibaba drops 7%
stories.deck: Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index closed down 1.3% on Thursday, and the Hang Seng Tech Index fell 2.4%, Reuters reported, as investors assessed the fallout from Nvidia’s unfolding leadership crisis. Alibaba dropped 7%, its biggest daily loss since August.
stories.summary: Hong Kong stocks fell on Thursday as investors assessed the potential fallout from the scandal surrounding Nvidia’s chief executive, Reuters reported. The Hang Seng Index closed down 1.3% and the Hang Seng Tech Index dropped 2.4%. Alibaba Group tumbled 7%, its biggest daily loss since August, on concerns that Chinese cloud operators could face tighter U.S. restrictions on access to advanced chips, the report said. Large-language-model startups Z.AI and Minimax lost 9% and 8% respectively. Conglomerate CK Hutchison lost 4% after it was reported to have paused a planned dual listing of retailer AS Watson Group. Thursday’s Hong Kong session ended well before Nvidia announced in the United States that it had accepted Jensen Huang’s resignation, so the moves reflect the week’s scandal rather than that later statement. Saxo chief investment strategist Charu Chanana said tighter U.S. chip restrictions could speed up domestic semiconductor substitution while making it harder for Chinese cloud companies to obtain advanced computing technology.
stories.why: Hong Kong is where many of China’s biggest tech names trade, so a sharp drop in Alibaba and other AI-related stocks is the first clear market verdict in Asia on the Nvidia crisis — and it came before Wall Street had even opened on the resignation.
stories.label: Reported + analysis
stories.note: These are Thursday’s Hong Kong closing figures, from a Reuters report republished by Business Recorder. The session ended about 3 a.m. ET, before Nvidia announced Huang’s resignation later on Thursday in the U.S. Chanana’s comment is an analyst’s view.

stories.headline: Hong Kong opens a Sun Yat-sen ‘images’ exhibition on the 160th anniversary of his birth
stories.deck: The Leisure and Cultural Services Department and Hong Kong Baptist University opened a special exhibition at the Dr Sun Yat-sen Museum on Thursday. It runs from Friday to July 7, 2027, with free admission, and brings together more than 80 artefacts and about 100 historical photographs and documents.
stories.summary: The Leisure and Cultural Services Department and Hong Kong Baptist University presented a special exhibition, “Timeless Impressions — The Shaping and Representation of Dr Sun Yat-sen’s Images,” at the Dr Sun Yat-sen Museum, with an opening ceremony on Thursday. The show, which the government said is the museum’s first to take Sun’s image as its curatorial theme, runs from Friday, Nov. 13, to July 7, 2027, with free admission. It brings together more than 80 pieces or sets of artefacts from the museum, HKBU and local private collections, and around 100 historical photographs, newspaper clippings and archival materials, including coins, stamps, sculptures and cartoons from China and abroad. Assistant Director of Leisure and Cultural Services (Heritage and Museums) Ng Chi-wo, speaking at the opening, said the exhibition traces how Sun’s image was shaped through pictures, texts and objects. Other officiating guests included HKBU Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences dean Daniel W. L. Lai; Peter B. Sun, a great-grandnephew of Sun Yat-sen and a museum expert adviser; acting HKBU university librarian Bethany Wilkes; and Hong Kong Museum of History director Joyce Ho. The museum, HKBU and the Hong Kong Public Libraries are also offering free lectures, guided tours, workshops and related displays at six public libraries.
stories.why: The exhibition is a rare, free look at how Sun’s image was built up in print, coins and photographs, opening on the 160th anniversary of his birth just as Beijing has also been marking the same commemoration.
stories.label: Official statement
stories.note: The exhibition’s public run begins Friday. This morning’s edition covered Xi Jinping’s remarks in Beijing on the anniversary; this item is the Hong Kong museum show, announced after that edition was compiled.

stories.headline: Hong Kong export volumes jump 36.1% in September, import volumes 30.7%
stories.deck: The Census and Statistics Department said Thursday that the volume of Hong Kong’s goods exports rose 36.1% year on year in September, and import volumes rose 30.7%. Export and import prices were also sharply higher, up 20.3% and 19.7%.
stories.summary: Hong Kong’s Census and Statistics Department said Thursday that, in September 2026, the volume of total exports of goods rose 36.1% from a year earlier and the volume of imports rose 30.7%. For the first nine months of 2026, export volumes were up 29.9% and import volumes up 30.1% compared with the same period in 2025. Compared with the second quarter, third-quarter export and import volumes rose 1.8% and 1.0% on a seasonally adjusted basis. Export prices rose 20.3% year on year in September and import prices rose 19.7%; for the first nine months the increases were 11.4% and 11.0%. The terms of trade index, which compares export and import prices, was up 0.5% in September and 0.4% in the first nine months. Among main destinations, export volumes to Taiwan rose 120.5%, to the United States 90.1%, to Vietnam 36.8% and to the Chinese mainland 34.7%, while exports to India fell 2.4%. Import volumes rose from all main suppliers, led by Korea (118.2%) and Vietnam (73.6%).
stories.why: The volume figures strip out price changes, so they show a real surge in goods moving through Hong Kong, not just inflation in the value of trade.
stories.label: Official figures
stories.note: The release was issued at 4:30 p.m. HKT (3:30 a.m. ET), before this morning’s edition was compiled, and is included here because it was not in that edition.

stories.deck: The Major Sports Events Committee awarded “M” Mark status on Thursday to the Hong Kong Open badminton championships, a FIBA 3x3 World Tour stop and the Hong Kong Squash Open, all scheduled over the next four weeks.
stories.summary: Hong Kong’s Major Sports Events Committee awarded “M” Mark status on Thursday to three upcoming international events: the LI-NING Hong Kong Open Badminton Championships 2026, part of the HSBC BWF World Tour Super 500, from Nov. 17 to 22; the FIBA 3x3 World Tour Hong Kong 2026, on Nov. 28 and 29; and the Milwaukee Hong Kong Squash Open 2026, from Nov. 30 to Dec. 6. stories.why: The designations lock in a dense run of world-level badminton, basketball and squash in Hong Kong over the next month, with official backing and, in some cases, public money.

stories.headline: ICAC charges Kai Tak Hospital site leader with taking more than $75,000 in bribes from imported workers
stories.deck: Hong Kong’s Independent Commission Against Corruption charged a subcontractor’s site team leader with accepting HK$75,100 in bribes from five electrical workers on the Kai Tak Hospital project. The case was due to be mentioned at Tuen Mun Magistrates’ Courts on Thursday.
stories.summary: The Independent Commission Against Corruption said it charged Zeng Chusong, 52, a site team leader for electrical subcontractor Billion Best (E&M) Engineering Company Limited on the Kai Tak Hospital construction project, with 10 counts of an agent accepting an advantage, contrary to the Prevention of Bribery Ordinance. The ICAC said the charges, laid on Wednesday night, allege that between September and November 2026 he accepted 10 bribes totalling HK$75,100 from five electrical workers for helping them get and keep jobs on the project, and that the case would be mentioned at Tuen Mun Magistrates’ Courts on Thursday morning. China State Construction Engineering (Hong Kong) Limited is the main contractor. The ICAC said China State Hong Kong had obtained importation quotas under the Labour Importation Scheme for the Construction Sector for subcontractors, including the defendant and the five workers he referred. The workers’ daily wage was $1,300, the commission said, and they paid him between $9,000 and $23,600 after being solicited for bribes and fearing the loss of their jobs. The ICAC said both companies prohibit staff from soliciting or accepting advantages, that they assisted the investigation, and that imported workers are offered corruption-prevention talks within eight weeks of arrival.
stories.why: The case, still only at the charge stage, puts a concrete figure on alleged kickbacks from imported construction workers on one of the city’s large public hospital projects.
stories.label: Allegation + official statement
stories.note: These are charges laid by the ICAC, not proven facts. The commission’s account of the payments and the workers’ fears is part of its case. The press release was issued around the Wednesday night charging and Thursday morning mention and was not in this morning’s edition.

stories.headline: China stocks slip and domestic chipmakers rally as investors assess the Nvidia scandal
stories.deck: The CSI 300 Index closed down 0.8% on Thursday and the Shanghai Composite fell 0.7%, Reuters reported, snapping a three-day advance. Shares in Moore Threads, MetaX and Cambricon each jumped more than 8% on expectations of faster domestic substitution.
stories.summary: Chinese mainland stocks snapped a three-day advance on Thursday as investors assessed the fallout from the scandal involving Nvidia’s chief executive, Reuters reported. The CSI 300 Index closed down 0.8% and the Shanghai Composite Index fell 0.7%. In contrast, shares in A-share-listed chip suppliers surged: Moore Threads, MetaX and Cambricon each jumped more than 8%, the report said, as the crisis boosted expectations that China would lean harder on domestic alternatives to Nvidia chips. Gold, game and robotics shares led the declines outside technology. Thursday’s mainland session, like Hong Kong’s, ended before Nvidia announced in the United States that it had accepted Jensen Huang’s resignation. Macquarie chief China economist Larry Hu was quoted as saying Chinese equities have been “disappointing” this year because of a lack of stimulus for domestic demand, and that the strength of exports heading into 2027 would help determine how much support Beijing provides.
stories.why: The split session — a softer benchmark, and a jump in Chinese AI-chip names — shows investors already trading a world in which Nvidia is under pressure, even before the resignation was announced in New York.
stories.label: Reported + analysis
stories.note: Closing figures are from a Reuters report republished by Business Recorder and cover Thursday’s session, which ended before the U.S. resignation announcement. Hu’s comment is an economist’s view.

stories.headline: China cuts gasoline and diesel prices from midnight, the first adjustment in two weeks
stories.deck: The National Development and Reform Commission said standard gasoline will fall 645 yuan a tonne and diesel 625 yuan a tonne from 24:00 on Nov. 12, or about 0.51 yuan a litre for 92-octane gasoline and 0.54 yuan a litre for No. 0 diesel.
stories.summary: China’s National Development and Reform Commission said Thursday that, from 24:00 on Nov. 12, the ceiling retail prices of standard gasoline and diesel would fall by 645 yuan and 625 yuan a tonne respectively, Xinhua reported. That works out to a cut of about 0.51 yuan a litre for 92-octane gasoline and 0.54 yuan a litre for No. 0 diesel. Under the domestic pricing mechanism, those ceilings are adjusted every 10 working days to follow a basket of international crude prices. Zhong Mijia of the NDRC’s price-monitoring centre said that although crude had risen slightly on Nov. 11, the 10-working-day average was still below the previous window, so domestic pump prices would be lowered. Xinhua said a typical private car would spend about 26 yuan less to fill a tank, and a large truck about 270 yuan less. The monitoring centre cautioned that geopolitical uncertainty, including the situation around Iran, could still move international oil prices.
stories.why: A 10-working-day price cut is one of the few official moves that shows up immediately at the pump, after a stretch of high international crude prices.
stories.label: Official statement + state media
stories.note: The Xinhua report was issued at 3:57 p.m. Beijing time (2:57 a.m. ET), before this morning’s edition, and is included here because it was not in that edition. The litre and “fill a tank” figures are the agency’s conversions and estimates. The comment on Iran and future oil prices is the monitoring centre’s analysis.

stories.headline: China’s second home-built large cruise ship finishes its first trial voyage in Guangzhou
stories.deck: Adora Flora City arrived at Guangzhou’s Nansha International Cruise Home Port on Thursday morning after a trial voyage from Shanghai, China Daily reported. A second trial is scheduled for Nov. 14 to 16, and commercial service is due to start from Guangzhou on Nov. 22.
stories.summary: Adora Flora City, China’s second domestically built large cruise ship, completed its first trial voyage and arrived at Guangzhou Nansha International Cruise Home Port on Thursday morning, China Daily reported. The ship, built by Shanghai Waigaoqiao Shipbuilding, a subsidiary of China State Shipbuilding Corporation, had left Shanghai’s Wusongkou International Cruise Terminal on Monday. Xinhua, in an earlier dispatch, said the voyage was meant to test navigation, safety, onboard services, ship-shore coordination and information systems, including stress tests of cabin, dining and entertainment operations. A second trial voyage is planned for Nov. 14 to 16, and the ship is scheduled to begin its inaugural season from Guangzhou on Nov. 22. China’s first domestically built large cruise ship, Adora Magic City, was delivered on Nov. 4, 2023.
stories.why: A second large cruise ship built in a Chinese yard is a test of whether the country can move from assembling one showpiece vessel to running a regular home-port operation.
stories.label: Reported + state media
stories.note: The arrival was reported by China Daily at 6:27 p.m. Beijing time (5:27 a.m. ET), just before this morning’s edition was compiled, and was not in that edition. The second trial and the Nov. 22 start of service are scheduled, not completed. The photo used here is of the first ship, Adora Magic City, not Flora City.

stories.headline: Chongqing opens its first fully automated metro express line
stories.deck: The Jingkou–Liangjiang Movie City section of Chongqing Rail Transit Line 15 began service on Thursday, China News Service reported. The 48-kilometre, 18-station stretch is the first section of a 72-kilometre express line designed to run at up to 140 km/h, and takes the city’s metro network past 600 kilometres.
stories.summary: Chongqing opened the first section of Rail Transit Line 15 on Thursday, China News Service reported. The Jingkou to Liangjiang Movie City section runs about 48 kilometres with 18 stations, from Jingkou in Shapingba District to Liangjiang Movie City in Liangjiang New Area, and is the first part of a 72-kilometre line with 25 stations and a design speed of 140 km/h — the fastest metro line in Chongqing’s central districts, the report said. Trains are six-car express sets. China News Service said the opening takes the city’s metro network officially past 600 kilometres.
stories.why: A fast, driverless east–west line through a mountainous city is a practical change for airport and high-speed-rail connections, not just another metro opening.

stories.headline: U.S. envoys meet Putin, then Zelenskyy, and claim a prisoner deal and a seat for Europe
stories.deck: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Vladimir Putin at the Kremlin on Thursday and later briefed Volodymyr Zelenskyy near Dublin. They and Zelenskyy said a large prisoner exchange had been finalised and that Europeans would join the next talks; a Kremlin aide was more cautious.
stories.summary: U.S. special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met President Vladimir Putin at the Kremlin on Thursday, then flew to Casement Aerodrome at Baldonnel, near Dublin, to brief President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. A Kremlin transcript of the opening of the Moscow meeting recorded Putin thanking them for helping to arrange contacts with Ukraine and pointing to a planned further step on prisoner exchanges, and recorded Witkoff describing the Abu Dhabi talks as positive and saying the prisoner swap would be “the largest one ever done.” After the Dublin meeting, Zelenskyy said there had been “real results,” that the prisoner exchange would be “the biggest exchange of war prisoners,” and that at the next meeting “Europeans will have a negotiation team at the table.” Kushner said the sides had been “able to finalise on the prisoner of war exchange” and that “thousands of people” would be returned to their families, and that Russia was “willing to give it a try” on a European role. Witkoff, speaking after the Moscow meeting, said “the Europeans will join at the next meeting,” Reuters reported, and that another trilateral round had been agreed. Kremlin aide Yury Ushakov was more cautious, Euronews reported: he said Europeans first needed to choose between “peace” or “war,” pointing to their military support for Ukraine, and that “so far, all their practical actions point precisely to the latter.” Putin, in the same session, argued that “grey zones” could not be the basis of a settlement and proposed a humanitarian evacuation in Kostiantynivka, which he said Russia controlled, as a test of who holds the ground. E.U. leaders are due to discuss on Friday whether to appoint a special envoy for the talks, Euronews said; Zelenskyy has asked them to designate a common representative by the end of the month. TASS, compiling official remarks, also quoted Putin as saying the presence of foreign troops in Ukraine was unacceptable, that any such forces would be a “legitimate target,” and that if European troops were deployed “the war would resume.”
stories.why: This morning’s edition could only report that the Kremlin meeting was scheduled; by evening the envoys had seen both Putin and Zelenskyy, claimed a landmark prisoner exchange, and run into a familiar gap between U.S. optimism and Moscow’s conditions on any European seat.
stories.label: Reported + official statement + state media
stories.note: Ongoing story: this morning’s edition reported that the envoys were going to the Kremlin after the Abu Dhabi talks. Witkoff’s, Kushner’s and Zelenskyy’s comments on a European seat at the next meeting are their statements; Ushakov’s remarks, as reported by Euronews, show Moscow has not given an unconditional yes. The next E.U. discussion of a special envoy is scheduled, not completed. TASS is Russian state media. A Kremlin opening transcript was also read during research; the linked TASS compilation covers the same official remarks.

stories.headline: Mercedes-Benz halts new investment at German plants and says closures are now under study
stories.deck: Mercedes-Benz told staff on Thursday that it is stopping all further investment at its German sites for now and will examine “in concrete and detailed terms” which plants it can still afford to keep, after talks on cutting costs stalled.
stories.summary: Mercedes-Benz announced on Thursday that it is halting all further investment at its German sites for the time being, Deutsche Welle reported, citing a memo from production board member Michael Schiebe on the company’s intranet that was seen by AFP. Board member Britta Seeger, in an intranet interview quoted by DW, said the company was “forced to examine, in concrete and detailed terms, which sites in Germany we can still afford to maintain,” while adding that “we all want to avoid plant closures at all costs” but “must now pursue this option in more concrete terms.” Schiebe said current cost structures made it impossible to invest in Germany and that German labour costs are sometimes five times higher than at plants in Eastern Europe. DW said he had recently warned that two plants in Germany — one assembly plant and one powertrain plant — would have to close unless costs were reduced. The report said Mercedes has been struggling with weaker demand in China, historically around a third of its passenger-car sales, with Chinese sales down about 19% in 2025; slower-than-expected demand for electric vehicles in Europe and North America; competition from cheaper Chinese EVs; and U.S. tariffs that the company has said cost it about €1 billion in profit last year. Volkswagen, BMW, Audi and Porsche have faced similar pressures, DW said.
stories.why: A halt to new investment by one of Germany’s signature manufacturers, and an explicit turn toward studying closures, is a sharper signal of how far the country’s auto slump has gone than another round of cost-cutting talks.
stories.label: Reported + official statement
stories.note: The halt and the study of closures were reported from an internal memo and interview, not from a formal public press release opened here. Closures have been put under study, not announced as decisions.

stories.headline: Infantino says Doha is safe for the U-17 World Cup after the United States withdraws
stories.deck: FIFA president Gianni Infantino told reporters in Doha on Thursday that “everyone is safe in Doha” after U.S. Soccer withdrew its team from the Under-17 World Cup, which kicks off on Nov. 19. FIFA said its own security assessment was unchanged.
stories.summary: FIFA president Gianni Infantino said in Doha on Thursday that Qatar is safe to host the Under-17 World Cup, after the United States withdrew its team over security concerns. “Every country, every national team knows best by themselves what they want to do, they decide,” he told Euronews and local media. “What I can say is that everyone is welcome in Doha, everyone is safe in Doha.” U.S. Soccer informed players on Wednesday that it was pulling out, citing security concerns in the Gulf and a U.S. Level 3 travel advisory, Euronews reported. FIFA confirmed the withdrawal on Thursday and said its security assessments “remain unchanged” and that “no new developments affecting the security situation around the tournament have occurred.” The United States had been drawn in Group J with Montenegro, Chile and Algeria. A replacement had not been announced; Jassim Al Jassim, chief executive of Qatar’s local organising committee, said he expected FIFA to announce something “within the next few days” and that preparations were continuing as normal, with several teams already in Doha. The tournament begins on Nov. 19, when hosts Qatar face Panama, and the final is scheduled for Dec. 13 at Ahmad bin Ali Stadium. It is the second of five consecutive U-17 World Cups Qatar is due to host through 2029.
stories.why: A U.S. withdrawal on security grounds, days before kickoff, leaves FIFA insisting the tournament is safe and a group-stage place still unfilled.
stories.label: Official statement + reported
stories.note: U.S. Soccer’s decision was conveyed to players on Wednesday; FIFA’s confirmation and Infantino’s comments came on Thursday. A replacement team had not been named when this edition was compiled. Kickoff on Nov. 19 is scheduled.

stories.headline: Pope Leo XIV, in Lima, urges Peruvians to “value women” and build a more inclusive society
stories.deck: On his first full day in Peru, Pope Leo XIV told a crowd in Lima’s cathedral square that families, cultural diversity, the dignity of women and fair work all have a part in the common good, and he condemned machismo and violence against women.
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV, on the first full day of his apostolic journey in Peru, spoke in the square in front of Lima’s Cathedral of Saint John the Apostle and Evangelist at a meeting on “Challenges and Hopes of the Peruvian People.” After listening to four testimonies, he said families, cultural diversity, the participation of women and dignified work all help build a society committed to the common good, and he called for solidarity, respect and an end to corruption, violence and individualism. On women’s rights he said, “Let us value women! Let us protect and respect girls!,” and he deplored machismo, the absence of fathers from family life, and abuse and violence against women, including the double marginalisation of women in poverty and in Indigenous and Afro-Peruvian communities. He described the family as the first natural society, warned that digital technology can replace genuine human contact, and said businesses should be “communities of dignified work and social responsibility,” while public authorities should provide a just legal framework. A later prayer vigil with young people and university students was scheduled at the National Stadium, according to his published itinerary.
stories.why: The new pope used his first full day in the country of his pastoral roots to put violence against women, family strain and informal work at the centre of a public address, not only a church service.
stories.label: Official statement
stories.note: The quotations are from the Vatican News account of the Lima cathedral-square meeting. The National Stadium vigil was listed on his schedule; this edition does not treat it as reported in detail unless sourced above.
